title: Positivity of the spectral norm bound
statement:
Let $k, d, \ell$ be positive integers and let $n \ge 2$. Then there exists a positive real constant $C_1 > 0$ for which the quantity
\[
  C_1 \cdot d \cdot \sqrt{k\,\ell\,\log n}
\]
is itself positive.
caveat: The Lean conclusion asserts only that a positive constant C₁ exists making the product C₁·d·√(k·ℓ·log n) positive; the "expected spectral norm" reading in the source comment is external context not carried by the formal statement, so it is not asserted.
replaced:
For naturals $k, d, \ell > 0$ and $n \ge 2$ there exists a real constant $C_1 > 0$ such
that
\[
  C_1 \cdot d \cdot \sqrt{k\,\ell\,\log n} \;>\; 0 .
\]
The displayed quantity is the matrix-Khintchine bound $\E_b[\norm{A}] \le
C_1\, d\, \sqrt{k\,\ell\,\log n}$ appearing in the argument, and the statement asserts
that such a positive constant, with positive associated bound, exists.
